_readme: WORKED EXAMPLE — Amazon product page. The pure-HTML case.
Target: /Disney-Cars-Radiator-Die-Cast-Vehicles/dp/B08J4FJ63D
Read off the live page with real Chrome on 2026-09-02. Counts and values are observed.
WHY THIS PAGE COMPLETES THE SET:
Zara    — JSON-LD ProductGroup, everything in one standard blob.
Walmart — no Product JSON-LD at all; a 352 KB __NEXT_DATA__ carries everything.
Amazon  — MEASURED: 0 JSON-LD scripts, no __NEXT_DATA__, no hydration globals.
Only 5 meta tags, none of them commercial (title, description,
encrypted-slate-token, bidi-endpoint, flow-closure-id).
There is NO structured data. Every field here is CSS or XPath, by necessity.
Together these three are why candidate ordering is per-field and per-page rather than a
global policy: 'prefer JSON-LD' is excellent advice that would collect nothing here.
WHAT MAKES THE SPECS HARD (all observed):
1. NO STABLE IDS. The documented Amazon ids — #productDetails_techSpec_section_1,
#detailBullets_feature_div, #productOverview_feature_div — are ALL ABSENT on this page.
Instead there are 7 anonymous <table class='a-keyvalue prodDetTable'>, 5 of which have
rows: 22, 8, 4, 4 and 1 — 39 spec rows in total.
2. THE ROWS ARE SPLIT ACROSS TWO CONTAINERS, and a complete spec map needs both:
#productDetails_expanderTables_depthLeftSections   -> 1 table,  22 rows
#productDetails_expanderTables_depthRightSections  -> 4 tables, 17 rows
Both sit under #productDetails_expanderSectionTables, which is the join point the
recipe uses.
3. HEADING-PROXIMITY LOCATORS DO NOT WORK HERE. While probing, a 'nearest preceding
heading' heuristic labelled four different spec tables 'Warranty & Support' — the
heading of an unrelated empty table earlier in the DOM. This is worth stating because
'find the table under the heading that says X' is the first thing both a human and an
LLM reach for, and on this page it silently mislabels most of the data.
4. THE VALUES ARE DIRTY. Observed verbatim in the 22-row table:
'Customer Reviews' = '4.9 4.9 out of 5 stars (13,222) var dpAcrHasRegisteredArcLink…'
That tail is INLINE JAVASCRIPT leaking into innerText. 'Best Sellers Rank' similarly
carries '(See Top 100 in Toys & Games)' navigation chrome. A spec map built by blindly
pairing th/td ships both. The recipe filters them explicitly rather than pretending
textContent is clean.
5. PRICE WAS EMPTY. '.a-price .a-offscreen' resolved to '' and #availability read
'This item cannot be shipped to your selected delivery location.' The page rendered
fine — it was geo-gated by delivery address. This is exactly the built_under /
proxy_region concern in recipe-operations.md D6: the same URL, fetched from a different
place, legitimately has no price. price is therefore NOT marked required, and carries a
not_empty assertion so a missing price surfaces as 'suspect' rather than as a silent
null or a failed run.

ROW SPLIT, CORRECTED AGAINST THE LIVE PAGE. An earlier draft of this recipe split each <tr> on a NEWLINE between key and value. Running the real reader against the real page showed textContent joins th and td with RUNS OF SPACES, not a newline: that pattern parsed 1 of 39 rows, and the one row it did parse was 'Customer Reviews', whose value carries a block of inline JavaScript. The recipe would have shipped a one-entry spec map full of JS and reported success. Splitting on the first run of 2+ whitespace parses 37 of 39, dropping exactly the two rows filtered on purpose. Observed separator widths ranged from 2 to 36 characters.
name: amazon-product
_sample_urls_note: One URL verified live. Amazon's detail-page layout varies enormously by category (books, electronics and apparel each use different spec containers), so this recipe needs sample URLs from several categories before leaving draft — more than the usual three.

dimensions._comment: A genuine Lua case: '3.15 x 3.54 x 1.18 inches' -> four typed fields. Three numbers and a unit cannot be produced by an ordered list of scalar ops without inventing a dozen of them.

weight.description: Item weight parsed into value and unit

name._comment: The <title> tag carries the same string wrapped in 'Amazon.com: … : Category'.

asin._comment: The URL is the most stable source on the entire page.
Also present as a spec row: 'ASIN' = 'B08J4FJ63D'. XPath earns its place here — selecting a <td> by its sibling <th>'s text is the one thing CSS cannot express.

price._comment: .a-offscreen is the accessible full price string. Observed EMPTY on a geo-gated load — the candidate is correct, the page had no price to give.

availability_text.note: Observed 'This item cannot be shipped to your selected delivery location.' — a geo-gate, not an out-of-stock. Keeping the raw text is what makes the two distinguishable downstream.

average_rating._comment: The title ATTRIBUTE is clean ('4.9 out of 5 stars'); the element's innerText is '4.9 \n4.9 out of 5 stars' — the same number twice. Reading the attribute avoids a de-duplication problem entirely.

feature_bullets._comment: Observed 5 bullets. Amazon pads them with zero-width marks (\u200e/\u200f), which strip_control removes.

_comment: THE FOUR CLICK-TO-EXPAND SECTIONS, plus 'Item details'. All five are:
MEASURED: clicking them grew document.body.innerText by +303 / +73 / +97 / +22 chars
for Features & Specs / Style / Measurements / Additional details.
AND YET no click is needed to READ them. Their rows are already in the DOM, merely
collapsed, so attribute='text' (textContent) returns them intact while attribute=
'visible_text' (innerText) would return nothing. See recipe-contract-v2.md section 2,
'text vs visible_text'. That is why this group has NO steps: five clicks were removed
after measuring that they changed the extracted values not at all.
The expand steps are retained below in _steps_if_visible_text_needed, commented out of
the live recipe, so the reasoning survives for whoever revisits this.

_steps_if_visible_text_needed.label: Expand one section — only necessary when reading visible_text

features_and_specs._comment: 8 rows observed: Power Source, Additional Features, Operation Mode, Scale, Battery Description, Number of Batteries, Educational Objective, Number of Players. The xpath anchors on the expander header's own text and walks to the sibling content — the only reliable way to tell these five identically-classed tables apart. A 'nearest preceding heading' heuristic mislabels four of them 'Warranty & Support'.

transform.source:
local k, val = v:match('^%s*(.-)%s%s+(.-)%s*$')
if not k or k == '' or val == '' then return nil end
k = k:gsub('%s+', ' ')
val = val:gsub('%s+', ' '):gsub('^%s*(.-)%s*$', '%1')
if val == '' then return nil end
return { name = k, value = val }

transform.source:
local k, val = v:match('^%s*(.-)%s%s+(.-)%s*$')
if not k or k == '' or val == '' then return nil end
k = k:gsub('%s+', ' ')
if k == 'Customer Reviews' or k == 'Best Sellers Rank' then return nil end
val = val:gsub('%s*var%s+dpAcr.*$', ''):gsub('%s+', ' ')
val = val:gsub('^%s*(.-)%s*$', '%1')
if val == '' then return nil end
return { name = k, value = val }

field_groups._comment: The merged view: 39 rows across 5 tables in 2 containers, as ONE key->value map. Same data as the five per-section fields above, flattened for callers who want a single spec sheet rather than the page's sectioning.

specifications._comment: repeat-free approach: one candidate returning all rows as {name,value} pairs, then to_object. The xpath selects tr elements that actually have BOTH th and td, which skips the header/spacer rows that would otherwise become empty keys.

transform._comment: A row's innerText is 'Key\nValue'. Split on the first newline, then drop the two rows observed to be polluted: 'Customer Reviews' carries inline JS ('var dpAcrHasRegisteredArcLinkClickAction'), 'Best Sellers Rank' carries navigation chrome. Returning nil drops the row.
